text:
alex (Product): Quick design check — putting the 'Horizon' selector + SLO slider in the Capacity modal. Figma: https://figma.redwood/horizon-capacity (commented). Can we do a quick pass on keyboard and microcopy? sasha (Design): skimmed — main thing is the label density. 'Horizon' is a weird word for some PMs. Maybe 'Capacity horizon' or 'Window' + short help text. omar (Frontend): keyboard rules we should support: arrow keys to adjust, shift+arrow to jump steps, Home/End to go to min/max, Enter to apply, Esc to cancel. Also numeric input fallback for screenreader users. kevin (Engineering): agree with keyboard. Also: slider should not commit changes until blur/enter — that avoids accidental spikes. We need a clear visual commit affordance (Apply button) when multiple fields editable. jordan (PM): copy thoughts for burst tooltip — current mock says "Burst: extra GPUs" which is vague. Suggest: "Burst capacity — temporary extra GPUs to handle short spikes. Billed at burst rate." Small link: "How billing works". sasha (Design): proposal for inline microcopy: under slider: "Target SLO (p50 latency). Lower = more capacity, higher cost." Keep it short. For the Horizon selector options: 1m, 5m, 1h, 24h with tooltips: "Window used to calculate autoscale signals." kevin (Engineering): UX edge: if Horizon is long (24h) we should show an estimation CTA: "Expected instance-hours per day" preview. Might be backend heavy but useful. omar (Frontend): a11y bits — use role=slider + aria-valuemin/max/now + aria-label that includes units. Example: ```
``` Also ensure the numeric input next to slider is keyboard focusable and labeled. sasha (Design): copy tweak: change "Burst" to "Burst capacity (temporary)" and change the confirm modal copy to: "Add burst capacity for up to X minutes. This will increase cost while active." Add a subtle caution icon. jordan (PM): guardrail idea: add a soft-warning when SLO < 50ms: "Aggressive SLO may increase costs; try 50–200ms for typical workloads." Maybe an inline pill: "Cost impact: high" with hover. kevin (Engineering): on guardrails — prefer helpful nudge over hard block. If user pushes below safe floor we show the nudge + link to cost estimator. Only block if there's safety concerns. a11y-bot: Accessibility checklist: 1) slider has accessible name + value announcement on change, 2) focus order: Horizon -> SLO slider -> numeric input -> min/max -> Burst toggle -> Apply/Cancel, 3) contrast for disabled/min labels >= 4.5:1, 4) keyboard shortcuts documented in help. sasha (Design): visual affordance note — when 'Auto scale' is toggled on, should we hide min/max or grey them but show tooltip? I'm leaning grey + tooltip: users expect the numbers still visible. omar (Frontend): implement grey + tooltip. Make disabled inputs reachable by screenreader and announce 'Auto-scale enabled, manual min/max disabled'. alex (Product): copy decision: keep 'Horizon' but add help icon text: "Horizon: time window for autoscale signals." Also change burst CTA to "Add temporary capacity". jordan (PM): ask: do we need a per-pool default? Users asked for per-pool presets in research. Could be a follow-up — not in this PR. sasha (Design): small layout nit — move numeric input to the right of slider and reduce gap, keeps visual compactness for small screens. kevin (Engineering): perf note: continuous slider events must debounce to 200ms before sending signals. Also ensure KV cache won't be flushed by minor SLO edits. a11y-bot: final: add link to internal a11y doc: /ops/accessibility/sliders and run axe in storybook. alex (Product): action items: Sasha — update copy + tooltips; Omar — keyboard/aria implementation; Kevin — debounce + cost preview API feasibility; Jordan — write PR context about guardrails. I'll queue for design review tomorrow. :+1: sasha (Design): ack, will update Figma and post new frame. kevin (Engineering): ack, will check API. oman (typo in thread): oops — meant Omar. jordan (PM): thanks everyone — landing next week if no blockers. :party_parrot:
